docs.title: RKO - Random-Key Optimizer
docs.text:
Welcome to the documentation for the modernized C++20 implementation of the RKO framework.

This framework is built around a Dynamic Plugin Architecture that decouples the core optimization engine in \([0, 1)^n\) from problem-specific logic. Users no longer need to recompile the solver to test new combinatorial optimization problems; they compile their problem as a shared library (.so or .dll) and load it at runtime.

docs.title: Architectural Scope
docs.text:
The framework is split into two major components:

  1. The Core Engine (rkosolver): Manages OpenMP multi-threading, 15 registered metaheuristics (14 active search/hybridization metaheuristics plus MultiStart), online Q-Learning parameter control with M/D/A adjacent topology and Q-Table persistence, multi-objective scalarization strategies with anti-drift re-scalarization, deterministic time-gated Nelder-Mead local search, and a thread-safe elite solution pool.
  2. The Problem Plugins (.so / .dll): Independent shared libraries that implement the IProblem interface (Decoder and IO).
flowchart LR
    CLI["CLI11 + YAML
(config.yaml, param-*.yaml)"] --> Solver["RkoSolver
(Central Orchestrator)"]
    Solver --> Threads["OpenMP Search Threads
15 Registered MHs + RVND / NM
Online Q-Learning"]
    Solver --> Context["SolverContext (Singleton)
Elite Pool (SOLVER_POOL)
Cache-Aligned PaddedRng"]
    Threads <-->|"pool_lock"| Context
    Threads --> Eval["decodeSolution() + IScalarizer
(Tchebycheff | WeightedSum | Gini | Lexicographic_MinMax)"]
    Context -->|"rescalarizePool()"| Eval
    Eval <-->|"dlopen / dlsym"| Plugin["Dynamic Problem Plugin (.so / .dll)
IProblem::load() & IProblem::decode()"]

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 15 Registered Metaheuristics: SA, ILS, EILS, VNS, GRASP, LNS, TS, BRKGA, BRKGA-CS, PSO, GA, DE, ACO, IPR, and MultiStart (see Metaheuristics Catalog).
  • Online Q-Learning Parameter Control (control_mode: 1): Reinforcement learning engine using \(O(|\mathcal{S}| \cdot m)\) adjacent M/D/A action topology, capped relative improvement (ComputeDelta, \(\delta_{\max} = 0.1\)), configurable exploration floor (\(\varepsilon_{\min} = 0.1\), or 0.05 in ACO), conditional UpdateMaxQ, and thread-safe Q-Table persistence (results/QTable_<method>.txt).
  • Deterministic Time-Gated Nelder-Mead & Decoupled RVND: RVND focuses strictly on SwapLS, InvertLS, and FareyLS, while NelderMeadSearch is triggered across all 13 search metaheuristics via configurable tau_min_nm and tau_max_nm time fractions with per-iteration improv = 0 resets.
  • Implicit Path-Relinking (IPR) with 6 Strategies: Contiguous block coverage supporting One-way, Back-and-Forth, Mixed, GRAPR, Truncated, and External trajectories, tuned online by an 18-state Q-Learning controller.
  • Multi-Objective Optimization & Anti-Drift Sync: Native support for single- and multi-objective problems with Tchebycheff, WeightedSum, Ideal/Nadir-normalized Gini_Coefficient, and Lexicographic_MinMax scalarizers, plus automatic pool re-scalarization whenever reference points shift.
  • Three Elite Pool Diversity Policies (poolUpdateMethod): Supports Cosine Similarity tactical replacement (0), NSGA-II non-dominated sorting & crowding distance (1), and Spatial Frontier Niche Geometry (2).
  • Thread-Safe Elite Solution Pool & IO: Synchronized via #pragma omp critical(pool_lock) with 64-byte cache-line-aligned PaddedRng generators and comprehensive output logs in results/.

docs.title: Building the Core Solver
docs.text:
The project uses CMake for the core engine and a Makefile for rapid plugin development.

From the repository root, run: 

make build
This creates the build/ directory, resolves dependencies (yaml-cpp, CLI11), and compiles the rkosolver binary in build/bin/rkosolver.

docs.title: Building a Problem Plugin
docs.text:
To compile a problem plugin (e.g., Tourist, Knapsack Problem, or TSP) without recompiling the core: 

make plugin PROB=tourist
# Or for the Knapsack Problem:
make plugin PROB=kpproblem
Compiled plugins are saved to build/plugins/.

docs.title: Running the Algorithm
docs.text:
The solver is executed from the project root via CLI, providing the instance file, configuration file, maximum execution time, and compiled plugin path.

Linux Example: 

./build/bin/rkosolver -i ./instances/tourist-1/I1.txt -c ./config/yaml/config.yaml -t 10 -p ./build/plugins/tourist.so

CLI Arguments: - -i, --instance: Path to the problem instance file. - -t, --time: Maximum execution time in seconds (MAXTIME). - -c, --config: Path to the YAML configuration file (defaults to config/yaml/config.yaml). - -p, --plugin: Path to the problem dynamic library (.so or .dll).

docs.title: Generated Output Files (results/)
docs.text:
Default configuration (config/yaml/param-*.yaml) and output paths (results/) are resolved relative to the project root:

File Description results/Results_RKO.csv Aggregated single-objective run statistics (best/mean OFV, runtime, discovery time). results/Results_MO_RKO.csv Aggregated multi-objective run statistics (scalarized OFV, raw objective vectors, runtime). results/Solutions_RKO.txt Detailed record of the global best solution, originating MH, raw objs, and random-key vector rk. results/Pool_Solutions_RKO.txt Full elite pool dump (OFV, originating MH, relative Best time, Objs, RK). results/Convergence_Log.csv Timestamped incumbent improvement trajectory across runs. results/QTable_<method>.txt Persisted Q-Table per metaheuristic when control_mode: 1 (auto-reloaded on compatible subsequent runs).

docs.title: Configuration (config/yaml/config.yaml)
docs.text:
# Selected Metaheuristics (Each runs in a dedicated OpenMP thread)
metaheuristics:
  - SA
  - ILS
  - VNS
  - BRKGA
  - BRKGA-CS
  - PSO
  - GA
  - LNS
  - GRASP
  - IPR
  - DE
  - TS
  - ACO
  - EILS

# General Execution Settings
execution_settings:
  max_runs: 10         # Maximum number of runs
  debug_mode: 0        # 0: File Output (CSV/TXT), 1: Terminal Debug Output
  control_mode: 1      # 0: Offline Tuning, 1: Online Control (Q-Learning)

# Search Parameters
search_parameters:
  local_search_strategy: 1  # 1: First Improvement, 2: Best Improvement
  restart_threshold: 1      # Fraction of max time to trigger restart
  elite_pool_size: 10       # Base size of the elite solution pool (2x for multi-objective)
  tau_min_nm: 0.005         # Minimum fraction of MAXTIME between Nelder-Mead calls
  tau_max_nm: 0.20          # Maximum fraction of MAXTIME without a Nelder-Mead call

# Multi-Objective Scalarization:
# "Tchebycheff", "WeightedSum", "Gini_Coefficient", or "Lexicographic_MinMax"
scalarization: "Gini_Coefficient"

# Decay factor for Lexicographic_MinMax (default: 0.05)
# lexicographic_decay: 0.05

# Default objective weights
default_weights: [0.50, 0.50]

# Optional A Priori Reference Points (calculated dynamically if omitted)
# ideal_point: [-110.0, 40.0]
# nadir_point: [0.0, 100.0]

# Freeze ideal / nadir points during search (true/false)
fixed_ideal_point: false
fixed_nadir_point: false

# Pool Update Strategy:
# 0 = Standard (Cosine Similarity Diversity), 1 = NSGA-II, 2 = Spatial Frontier Niche Geometry
poolUpdateMethod: 0

Parameter Ordering for Online Control

When using control_mode: 1, candidate lists in config/yaml/param-online.yaml should be sorted in ascending order so that Q-Learning Decrease (D) and Increase (A) actions correspond to true parameter decrements and increments.

docs.title: Creating a New Problem Plugin
docs.text:
To solve a new problem, implement the rkolib::core::IProblem interface:

  1. Create a .cpp file in problems/ (e.g., myproblem.cpp).
  2. Include rkolib/core/problem.hpp and implement load(), decode(TSol &sol) const, getDimension(), and getNumObjectives():
#include "rkolib/core/problem.hpp"

class MyProblem : public rkolib::core::IProblem {
public:
    void load(const std::string &filename) override {
        // Read instance data from file
    }

    void decode(rkolib::core::TSol &sol) const override {
        // Transform random-key vector sol.rk into a feasible solution
        // Store raw objective values in sol.objs (canonical minimization convention)
    }

    int getDimension() const override { return 100; }
    int getNumObjectives() const override { return 2; }
};

// Export plugin factory functions via C linkage
REGISTER_RKO_PROBLEM(MyProblem)
  1. Build and run your plugin: 
    make plugin PROB=myproblem
./build/bin/rkosolver -i ./instances/myproblem/inst1.txt -c ./config/yaml/config.yaml -t 10 -p ./build/plugins/myproblem.so

docs.title: Parallel Execution & Synchronization
docs.text:
• OpenMP Thread Allocation: Each selected metaheuristic executes independently in its own OpenMP thread alongside a dedicated reference-point and time-monitoring thread.
  • False-Sharing Protection (PaddedRng): Per-thread std::mt19937 engines are 64-byte cache-line aligned (alignas(64)) in SolverContext to prevent L1/L2 cache contention.
  • Dedicated Acyclic Critical Sections:
  • #pragma omp critical(pool_lock) protects all reads/writes to SOLVER_POOL (CreatePoolSolutions, UpdatePoolSolutions, NelderMeadSearch, IPR, and rescalarizePool).
  • #pragma omp critical(scalarization_lock) protects dynamic updates to idealPoint_, nadirPoint_, and scalarizer invocations inside decodeSolution.
  • #pragma omp critical(qtable_io_lock) serializes SaveQTable and LoadQTable file access.

For deep dives into Q-Learning, Nelder-Mead/RVND, IPR, scalarization mathematics, and all 15 metaheuristics, see Algorithms & Control, Metaheuristics Catalog, and the full LaTeX Technical Manual.

docs.title: Algorithms & Control Mechanisms
docs.text:
This page documents the transversal mathematical and algorithmic mechanisms shared across RKOSolver: Online Q-Learning, Local Search (RVND & Time-Gated NelderMeadSearch), Implicit Path-Relinking (IPR), Multi-Objective Scalarization, and Elite Pool Diversity Management.

For individual algorithm mechanics and parameter grids of all 15 registered metaheuristics, see the Metaheuristics Catalog.

docs.title: 1. Online Q-Learning Parameter Control
docs.text: When control_mode: 1 is enabled in config/yaml/config.yaml, each metaheuristic adapts its hyperparameters online by navigating a discrete Markov Decision Process (MDP) over parameter configurations.

docs.title: 1.1 M/D/A Adjacent Action Topology
docs.text:
Each parameter \(j \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}\) has an ordered list of candidate values \(P_j = \{v_{j,0} < \dots < v_{j,n_j - 1}\}\), forming the Cartesian state space \(\mathcal{S} = P_0 \times \dots \times P_{m-1}\) of size \(|\mathcal{S}| = \prod_{j=0}^{m-1} n_j\). Rather than connecting every state to all Hamming-distance-1 neighbors in \(O(|\mathcal{S}|^2)\), CreateStates builds an adjacent transition graph via stride in \(O(|\mathcal{S}| \cdot m)\):

\[\text{stride}[j] = \frac{|\mathcal{S}|}{\prod_{r=0}^{j} n_r}, \qquad c_j(i) = \left\lfloor \frac{i}{\text{stride}[j]} \right\rfloor \bmod n_j\]
  • Maintain (M): Stay in the current state \(i \to i\).
  • Decrease (D): Step one parameter \(j\) down to \(v_{j, c_j(i) - 1}\) (i - stride[j]) when \(c_j(i) > 0\).
  • Increase (A): Step one parameter \(j\) up to \(v_{j, c_j(i) + 1}\) (i + stride[j]) when \(c_j(i) < n_j - 1\).

Every state therefore has between \(1 + m\) (grid corners) and \(1 + 2m\) (interior states) feasible actions (initialized with optimistic priors \(Q_0(s, a) \sim \mathcal{U}(0.005, 0.01)\)), ensuring smooth, physically meaningful parameter transitions.

docs.title: 1.2 Capped Relative Improvement (ComputeDelta) and Exploration Floor
docs.text:
To prevent a single large jump (e.g., leaving a penalized infeasible region or crossing zero) from collapsing exploration \(\varepsilon \to 0\), relative improvement is computed by ComputeDelta:

\[\delta = \min\!\left(\frac{f^*_{\text{old}} - f^*_{\text{new}}}{|f^*_{\text{old}}|}, \; \delta_{\max}\right), \quad \delta_{\max} = 0.1\]
  • Returns 0.0 if \(f^*_{\text{new}} \ge f^*_{\text{old}}\).
  • Returns \(\delta_{\max} = 0.1\) if \(f^*_{\text{new}} < f^*_{\text{old}}\) and \(|f^*_{\text{old}}| < 10^{-12}\).

Before choosing the next action, SetQLParameter updates \(\varepsilon\), learning rate \(\alpha_t\) (lf), and discount factor \(\gamma\) (df):

\[\varepsilon \leftarrow \max\!\big(\varepsilon_{\min}, \; \varepsilon \cdot (1 - \text{clamp}(\delta, 0, 1))\big)\] \[\text{lf} = \max\!\left(0.01, \; 1.0 - 0.9 \cdot \frac{t}{\text{MAXTIME}}\right), \qquad \text{df} = 0.8\]

where \(\varepsilon_{\min} = 0.10\) by default (0.05 in ACO). Depending on the metaheuristic's temporal granularity, Q-Learning actions and rewards operate either per iteration/generation (e.g., SA, ILS, LNS, TS, BRKGA, BRKGA-CS, GA, PSO, DE, ACO, IPR) or per complete multi-step cycle (VNS over \(k=1..k_{\max}\), GRASP over grid scales \(h_s \to h_e\), and EILS over its 5 perturbation levels).

docs.title: 1.3 Bellman Update & Conditional UpdateMaxQ
docs.text:
After observing reward \(R\), UpdateQValue transitions \(s_t \to s_{t+1} = \text{Ai}[s_t][a_t]\) and applies the Bellman update:

\[Q(s_t, a_t) \leftarrow Q(s_t, a_t) + \text{lf} \cdot \big(R + \text{df} \cdot \max_{a'} Q(s_{t+1}, a') - Q(s_t, a_t)\big)\]
  • If the updated \(Q(s_t, a_t) > \text{maxQ}(s_t)\), both maxQ and maxA are updated in \(O(1)\).
  • Only when the previously greedy action (at == S[st].maxA) decreases in value does UpdateMaxQ rescan S[st].Qa in \(O(|\text{Ai}|)\).

docs.title: 1.4 Q-Table Persistence (SaveQTable / LoadQTable)
docs.text:
• At startup (right after CreateStates), each online metaheuristic calls LoadQTable(S, method) to check results/QTable_<method>.txt.
  • The file is loaded only if the saved topology (numStates, numPar, parameter values per state, and action targets Ai) matches the current state space within \(10^{-6}\).
  • On exit (including time-limit termination via SOLVER_SHOULD_STOP), SaveQTable(S, st, method) persists the learned Q-Table under #pragma omp critical(qtable_io_lock).

docs.title: 2.1 Decoupled RVND
docs.text:
RVND (src/core/method.cpp) explores three fast random-key neighborhoods over a shuffled permutation RKorder, resetting the active neighborhood list whenever an improvement is found and honoring local_search_strategy (1 = First Improvement, 2 = Best Improvement):

  1. SwapLS: Pairwise swap of random-key positions (\(O(n^2)\)).
  2. InvertLS: Complementary mirror inversion \(r_k \leftarrow 1.0 - r_k\) (\(O(n)\)).
  3. FareyLS: Sampling across the 18 subintervals of the order-7 Farey sequence \(\mathcal{F}_7\) (\(18n\) evaluations).

NelderMeadSearch is decoupled from RVND so it never inflates the cost of inner local-search calls.

docs.title: 2.2 Time-Gated NelderMeadSearch Trigger & Feedback Injection
docs.text:
Across all 13 search metaheuristics (SA, ILS, EILS, VNS, GRASP, LNS, TS, BRKGA, BRKGA-CS, GA, PSO, DE, ACO), NelderMeadSearch builds a 3-vertex simplex using two elite solutions sampled under pool_lock from SOLVER_POOL and executes deterministically based on elapsed time (\(\Delta t_{\text{NM}}\)):

double deltaT_NM = currentTime - lastNM_time;
if ((improv && deltaT_NM >= tauMinNM_sec) || (deltaT_NM >= tauMaxNM_sec)) {
    NelderMeadSearch(targetSol, solver);
    currentTime = static_cast<float>(get_time_in_seconds() - start_timeMH);
    lastNM_time = currentTime;
}
  • Per-Iteration improv = 0 Reset: Every metaheuristic resets improv = 0 at the top of each iteration/generation, ensuring that even in offline mode (control_mode: 0), improv == 1 strictly reflects a fresh improvement rather than firing continuously every tau_min_nm.
  • Population & Trajectory Feedback:
  • Trajectory MHs (SA, ILS, VNS, GRASP, LNS, TS) apply NelderMeadSearch directly to the active working trajectory (s or sCurrent) before evaluating the Q-Learning reward.
  • Population/Swarm MHs (GA, PSO, BRKGA, BRKGA-CS, DE, ACO) refine the elite incumbent and feed improvements back into the active population (Pop[pos1] = bestInd in GA, Pbest[chosen] = Gbest in PSO, Pop[0] in BRKGA/BRKGA-CS, archive[0] in ACO).

docs.title: 3. Implicit Path-Relinking (IPR)
docs.text: IPR (src/mh/ipr.cpp) runs concurrently on its own OpenMP thread, pairing distinct elite solutions \((x^s, x^g)\) sampled from SOLVER_POOL under #pragma omp critical(pool_lock). If the pool has fewer than 2 solutions at startup, the thread waits cooperatively instead of terminating.

docs.title: 3.1 Contiguous Block Partitioning
docs.text:
Given dimension \(n\) and block fraction \(\alpha \in \{0.05, 0.10, 0.20\}\):

\[b = \max(1, \lfloor \alpha n \rfloor), \qquad m = \left\lceil \frac{n}{b} \right\rceil = \frac{n + b - 1}{b}\]

Each block \(\ell \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}\) covers the contiguous slice \([\ell b, \min((\ell + 1)b, n))\), ensuring 100% key coverage even when \(n\) is not divisible by \(b\).

docs.title: 3.2 Six Path-Relinking Strategies
docs.text: ID Enum Strategy Behavior 0 PR_ONE_WAY One-way Greedy internal path \(x^s \to x^g\) (\(d - 1\) steps). 1 PR_BACK_FORTH Back-and-Forth Evaluates both \(x^s \to x^g\) and \(x^g \to x^s\), keeping the best visited solution. 2 PR_MIXED Mixed Alternates greedy moves from both ends (\(s_A \to s_B\), \(s_B \to s_A\)) until meeting in the middle. 3 PR_GRAPR GRAPR Randomized greedy One-way selecting from an RCL of the top $\lceil 0.3 4 PR_TRUNCATED Truncated Greedy One-way stopped after \(\max(1, \lceil 0.5 d \rceil)\) moves. 5 PR_EXTERNAL External Greedy external path moving away from \(x^g\) (\(x_k \leftarrow \text{clamp}(1.0 - x_k^g, 0, 0.999999)\)) for \(d\) steps.

docs.title: 3.3 Online Q-Learning in IPR
docs.text:
• Offline (control_mode: 0): Uses \(\alpha = 0.10\) and PR_ONE_WAY.
  • Online (control_mode: 1): Controls an 18-state space (\(\alpha \in \{0.05, 0.10, 0.20\} \times \text{typePR} \in \{0, \dots, 5\}\)) with binary reward (evaluated when numDiff > 0):
\[r_t = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if } f(x^*_{\text{path}}) < \min(f(x^s), f(x^g)), \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}\]

docs.title: 4. Multi-Objective Scalarization & Reference Point Sync
docs.text:
All multi-objective scalarizers follow the canonical minimization convention (maximization objectives are negated by the problem decoder) and normalize raw objective vectors using the Ideal (\(z^*\)) and Nadir (\(z^{\text{nad}}\)) reference points:

\[d_i = w_i \cdot \max\!\left(0.0, \; \frac{f_i(x) - z^*_i}{\max(10^{-9}, \; z^{\text{nad}}_i - z^*_i)}\right)\]
  1. Tchebycheff (NormalizedWeightedTchebycheff): $\(F(x) = \max_{i} d_i + 10^{-4} \sum_{i} \frac{\max(0.0, \; f_i(x) - z^*_i)}{\max(10^{-9}, \; z^{\text{nad}}_i - z^*_i)}\)$
  2. WeightedSum (WeightedSumScalarizer): $\(F(x) = \sum_{i} w_i \cdot f_i(x)\)$
  3. Gini_Coefficient (GiniScalarizer): Minimizes mean normalized weighted regret combined with Gini inequality across objectives (Sen welfare form, singularity-free and Pareto-monotonic): $\(F(x) = \bar{d} \cdot (1 + G(d)) = \frac{1}{M}\sum_{i=0}^{M-1} d_i + \frac{1}{2 M^2} \sum_{i=0}^{M-1} \sum_{j=0}^{M-1} |d_i - d_j|\)$
  4. Lexicographic_MinMax (LexicographicMinMaxScalarizer): Sorts normalized weighted regrets in descending order \(d_{(0)} \ge d_{(1)} \ge \dots \ge d_{(M-1)}\) and aggregates them with geometric decay \(\gamma = \text{lexicographic\_decay}\) (default 0.05) plus a Pareto tie-breaking regularization tail: $\(F(x) = \sum_{r=0}^{M-1} \gamma^{r} d_{(r)} + \frac{10^{-6}}{M} \sum_{r=1}^{M-1} d_{(r)}\)$

docs.title: Anti-Drift Reference Point Management
docs.text:
• Two-Pass Pool Initialization: CreatePoolSolutions first decodes all initial candidates to consolidate non-degenerate \(z^*\) and \(z^{\text{nad}}\) bounds (ignoring penalized outliers \(\ge 10^{12}\)), and then re-scalarizes all solutions under the unified bounds.
  • Exponential Pool-Nadir Smoothing & rescalarizePool: During optimization, the monitor thread tracks \(z^*\) improvements and smooths \(z^{\text{nad}}\) from the non-dominated elite pool (\(0.8 z^{\text{nad}} + 0.2 z^{\text{nad}}_{\text{pool}}\)), invoking SolverContext::rescalarizePool whenever reference points shift so no stale ofv survives in SOLVER_POOL.

docs.title: 5. Elite Pool Diversity Policies (poolUpdateMethod)
docs.text:
Every candidate submitted to UpdatePoolSolutions must first pass a Global Guardian Filter that rejects objective/OFV clones (\(|\Delta| \le 10^{-9}\)) and strictly Pareto-dominated solutions (\(M > 1\)). Accepted candidates update SOLVER_POOL (capacity \(P = \text{sizePool}\) for \(M=1\), or \(P = 2 \cdot \text{sizePool}\) for \(M > 1\)) under one of three policies:

  • 0 — Tactical Cosine Similarity Replacement (Default): If \(f(s) < f(\text{Pool}[P-1])\), replaces the individual in the lower half of the pool (\(\lfloor P/2 \rfloor \le i < P\) with \(f(\text{Pool}[i]) > f(s)\)) that maximizes cosine similarity \(\cos(s.\text{rk}, \text{Pool}[i].\text{rk})\), preserving diverse genetic structures.
  • 1 — NSGA-II Pareto Ranking & Crowding Distance: Merges \(\text{Pool} \cup \{s\}\), performs Fast Non-Dominated Sorting (\(\mathcal{F}_1, \mathcal{F}_2, \dots\)) and Crowding Distance assignment, and retains the top \(P\) individuals.
  • 2 — Spatial Frontier Niche Geometry (\(M \ge 2\)): Projects solutions onto the chord connecting extreme Pareto anchors \((E_0, E_1)\), partitioning \([0, 1]\) into \(K = 5\) niches of capacity \(C = \lceil P / K \rceil\). Under-populated niches evict the worst orthogonal-distance point from overcrowded niches to fill gaps along the Pareto front.

docs.title: Metaheuristics Catalog
docs.text:
RKOSolver registers 15 metaheuristics in RkoSolver::initializeRegistry() (src/mh/), all operating purely on continuous random-key vectors \(\mathbf{x} \in [0, 1)^n\) and conforming to the uniform signature:

void MH(const rkolib::core::TRunData &runData, rkolib::RkoSolver &solver);

Each active metaheuristic listed in config/yaml/config.yaml executes asynchronously in its own dedicated OpenMP thread, cooperating through the thread-safe SOLVER_POOL.

docs.title: 1.1 Simulated Annealing (SA — src/mh/sa.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (5): \(SA_{\max}, \alpha_{\text{SA}}, \beta_{\min}, \beta_{\max}, T_0\).
  • Mechanics: At each temperature \(T\), executes \(SA_{\max}\) Metropolis steps perturbing the current solution s with ShakeSolution(betaMin, betaMax) and accepting worsening moves (\(\Delta > 0\)) with probability \(\exp(-\Delta / T)\).
  • Intensification & Reannealing: Before Q-Learning reward evaluation and geometric cooling (\(T \leftarrow \alpha_{\text{SA}} T\)), evaluates the time-gated NelderMeadSearch(s, solver) directly on s (marking improv = 1 if sBest improves). Cools until \(T \le 10^{-5}\) (0.00001), then reanneals at \(T \leftarrow 0.5 \, T_0\).
  • Online Reward: \(R = 1\) if sBest improved in the epoch; otherwise \((f(\mathbf{s}_{\text{Best}}) - f_{\text{bestEpoch}}) / (|f_{\text{bestEpoch}}| + 10^{-9})\).

docs.title: 1.2 Iterated Local Search (ILS — src/mh/ils.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (2): \(\beta_{\min}, \beta_{\max}\).
  • Mechanics: Generates an initial random-key vector refined immediately by RVND to initialize both the accepted local optimum sCurrent and the global incumbent sBest. Each iteration perturbs sCurrent via ShakeSolution(betaMin, betaMax) and applies RVND to obtain sBestLine.
  • Restart Acceptance & Intensification: Uses ILS_ACCEPT_RESTART, updating sCurrent = sBestLine whenever \(f(\mathbf{s}_{\text{BestLine}}) < f(\mathbf{s}_{\text{Current}})\) or after ILS_MAX_NO_IMPROV = 10 stagnant iterations (Iter - IterImprov >= 10). Time-gated NelderMeadSearch acts directly on sCurrent (resetting IterImprov if improved).
  • Online Reward: Binary reward \(R \in \{0, 1\}\) per iteration.

docs.title: 1.3 Enhanced Iterated Local Search (EILS — src/mh/eils.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (3): \(\beta_{\min}, \beta_{\max}, N_{\max}\).
  • Mechanics: Maintains an elite local optimum \(\mathbf{s}^*\) (sBest, initialized via RVND) and escalates perturbation across \(L = 5\) deterministic linear levels (EILS_NUM_LEVELS = 5):
\[\beta_\ell = \beta_{\min} + \ell \cdot \frac{\beta_{\max} - \beta_{\min}}{L - 1}, \qquad \ell \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}\]
  • Level Escalation Schedule: Every iteration perturbs \(\mathbf{s}^*\) with fixed intensity \(\beta_\ell\) (ShakeSolution(sLine, beta, beta, n)), applies RVND, and checks time-gated NelderMeadSearch(sBest, solver). Any strict improvement over \(\mathbf{s}^*\) sets cycleImprov = 1 and immediately restarts a fresh cycle at \(\ell = 0\); otherwise numFail increments, advancing \(\ell \leftarrow \ell + 1\) after \(N_{\max}\) consecutive failures and completing the cycle once \(\ell = 5\).
  • Cycle-Synchronized Q-Learning: Selects \((\beta_{\min}, \beta_{\max}, N_{\max})\) at the start of each level cycle (Maintain on the first cycle) and updates \(Q(s_t, a_t)\) at cycle completion with binary reward \(R = \text{cycleImprov} \in \{0, 1\}\).

docs.title: 1.4 Variable Neighborhood Search (VNS — src/mh/vns.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (2): \(k_{\max}, \beta_{\min}\).
  • Initialization: Samples 10 random initial solutions and initializes both sBest and s with the best candidate.
  • Mechanics: Iterates over neighborhoods \(k \in \{1, \dots, k_{\max}\}\), sampling \(\beta \sim \mathcal{U}(k\beta_{\min}, (k+1)\beta_{\min})\), perturbing s via ShakeSolution(beta, beta), and applying RVND. Accepts any improvement over s (resetting \(k \leftarrow 1\) when sBest improves; otherwise \(k \leftarrow k + 1\)).
  • Inner Intensification & Reward: Evaluates the deterministic NelderMeadSearch(s, solver) trigger inside the inner while (k <= kMax) loop using per-step iterImprov, while accumulating cycleImprov for the Q-Learning reward at the end of the neighborhood cycle.

docs.title: 1.5 Continuous Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure (GRASP — src/mh/grasp.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (3): \(\alpha_{\text{GRASP}}, h_s, h_e\).
  • Bidirectional Grid LineSearch: For coordinate \(i\) and step \(h\), builds the full candidate grid \(\{s_i\} \cup \{s_i \pm \tau h \in [0, 1) : \tau = 1, \dots, \lceil 1/h \rceil\}\), shuffles it via SOLVER_RNG, and evaluates \(q = \min(|\text{grid}|, \lceil \log_2(\lfloor 1/h \rfloor) \rceil + 1)\) candidates.
  • Randomized Adaptive Reconstruction: Partially randomizes \(\lceil n \cdot \mathcal{U}(0.3, 0.7) \rceil\) keys (UnFixed). At each constructive step, evaluates \(k_{\max} = \max(2, \lfloor 0.1 |\text{UnFixed}| \rfloor)\) unfixed coordinates via LineSearch, builds \(\text{RCL} = \{i : g_i \le g_{\min} + \alpha_{\text{GRASP}}(g_{\max} - g_{\min})\}\), and fixes one randomly chosen RCL coordinate.
  • Scale Halving & Inner Intensification: Applies RVND to the constructed solution; halves \(h \leftarrow h / 2\) whenever sBest does not improve, updates working solution s via greedy + linear Metropolis acceptance \(T = 100(1 - t / (T_{\max} \cdot \text{restart}))\), and checks time-gated NelderMeadSearch(s, solver) at every scale step \(h \ge h_e\).
  • Control Modes: Offline mode randomizes \(\alpha_{\text{GRASP}} \sim \mathcal{U}(0.1, 0.9)\) per step; online Q-Learning tunes 12 states with binary reward \(R \in \{0, 1\}\).

docs.title: 1.6 Large Neighborhood Search (LNS — src/mh/lns.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (4): \(\beta_{\min}, \beta_{\max}, T_0, \alpha_{\text{LNS}}\).
  • Mechanics: Destroys \(I \in [\lfloor \beta_{\min} n \rfloor, \lfloor \beta_{\max} n \rfloor]\) randomly chosen keys and repairs each key greedily by sampling inside the 18 subintervals of the Farey sequence \(\mathcal{F}_7\). Uses SA-style acceptance (cooling until \(T \le 0.01\), reannealing at \(0.3 \, T_0\)) and time-gated NelderMeadSearch(s, solver).

docs.title: 1.7 Tabu Search (TS — src/mh/ts.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (5): \(\text{maxNoImprovement}, \text{tabuTenure}, \text{neighborhoodSize}, \beta_{\min}, \beta_{\max}\).
  • Mechanics: Evaluates \(\lfloor n^2 \cdot \text{neighborhoodSize} \rfloor\) pairwise swap moves \((i, j)\). A swap is forbidden if \((i, j)\) or \((j, i)\) is active in tabuList (\(\text{iter} < \text{expiration}\)), unless it satisfies the aspiration criterion (\(f(\mathbf{s}_{\text{viz}}) < f(\mathbf{s}_{\text{Best}})\)).
  • Diversification & Reward: Applies the best admissible swap, records \(\{i^*, j^*, \text{iter} + \text{tabuTenure}\}\) while purging expired entries, triggers ShakeSolution(betaMin, betaMax) when \(\text{noImp} \ge \text{maxNoImprovement}\), refines via RVND, and checks time-gated NelderMeadSearch. Online reward: \(R = 1.0\) on global improvement, or \(R = -0.01\) otherwise.

docs.title: 2.1 Biased Random-Key Genetic Algorithm (BRKGA — src/mh/brkga.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (4): \(p, p_e, p_m, \rho_e\) (with dynamic UpdatePopSize).
  • Hybrid PUX Crossover: Copies the top \(\lfloor p \cdot p_e \rfloor\) elite individuals, generates \(\lfloor p(1 - p_e - p_m) \rfloor\) offspring via Parametric Uniform Crossover (PUX), and injects \(\lfloor p \cdot p_m \rfloor\) random mutants. In PUX, nonEliteParent is sampled 50% of the time from \([\text{eliteSize}, p - 1]\) and 50% of the time from the full population \([0, p - 1]\), swapping parents if Pop[eliteParent].ofv > Pop[nonEliteParent].ofv so \(\rho_e\) always favors the fitter parent. Applies time-gated NelderMeadSearch to Pop[0].

docs.title: 2.2 BRKGA with Community Search (BRKGA-CS — src/mh/brkga_cs.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (4): \(p, p_e, p_m, \rho_e\).
  • Community Detection & Selective RVND: Whenever an improvement occurs or stagnation exceeds 10 generations, builds a Pearson correlation graph (\(\sigma > 0.6\)) across the elite set and runs Label Propagation (LP) clustering. Non-representative elite members undergo chaotic mutation ChaoticInd (re-sampling keys with probability \(1 - \rho_e\) using fractional double rhoe), while RVND refines the top promising community representative (i < 1), complemented by time-gated NelderMeadSearch on Pop[0].

docs.title: 2.3 Genetic Algorithm (GA — src/mh/ga.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (3): \(\text{sizePop}, p_{\text{cros}}, p_{\text{mut}}\).
  • Mechanics: Binary tournament selection, uniform crossover (\(p_{\text{cros}}\)), gene-wise uniform mutation (\(p_{\text{mut}}\)), and generational replacement. Whenever time-gated NelderMeadSearch improves bestInd, the refined individual is injected back into a random slot of Pop (Pop[pos1] = bestInd).

docs.title: 2.4 Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO — src/mh/pso.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (4): \(P_{\text{size}}, c_1, c_2, w\).
  • Mechanics: Evolves particle positions \(\mathbf{X}_i \in [0, 1)^n\) and velocities \(\mathbf{V}_i\) toward personal bests \(\mathbf{P}_{\text{best}, i}\) and global best \(\mathbf{G}_{\text{best}}\). Whenever time-gated NelderMeadSearch improves \(\mathbf{G}_{\text{best}}\), the refined vector is injected into a random slot of Pbest (Pbest[chosen] = Gbest) to propagate elite genetic information across the swarm.

docs.title: 2.5 Differential Evolution (DE — src/mh/de.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (3): \(\text{sizePop}, Cr, F\) (with dynamic UpdatePopulationDE).
  • Hybrid Mutation & Toroidal Repair: For each target vector \(\mathbf{x}_i\), selects three distinct indices \(r_1, r_2, r_3 \ne i\) and \(j_{\text{rand}} \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}\). Under binomial crossover (\(u \le Cr \lor j = j_{\text{rand}}\)), alternates 50/50 between DE/rand/1 and DE/current-to-best/1, wrapping out-of-bounds keys toroidally via \(\text{trial}_j = \text{clamp}(v_j - \lfloor v_j \rfloor, 0, 0.9999999)\).
  • Refinement & Acceptance: Applies RVND to 5% of trial vectors, accepts improvements or Metropolis moves under linear cooling \(T = 1000(1 - t / (T_{\max} \cdot \text{restart}))\), and applies time-gated NelderMeadSearch on bestInd.

docs.title: 2.6 Continuous Ant Colony Optimization (ACO / \(\text{ACO}_{\mathbb{R}}\) — src/mh/aco.cpp)
docs.text:
• Controlled Parameters (4): \(k = \text{archive\_size}, m = \text{num\_ants}, q, \xi\) (\(\varepsilon_{\min} = 0.05\), binary reward \(R \in \{0, 1\}\)).
  • Gaussian Solution Archive: Maintains a sorted archive \(T = (\mathbf{s}_1, \dots, \mathbf{s}_k)\) with rank-based Gaussian weights \(\omega_l = \frac{1}{q k \sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\!\big(-\frac{(l - 1)^2}{2 q^2 k^2}\big)\). Each of the \(m\) ants selects a guide \(\mathbf{s}_l\) proportionally to \(\omega_l\) and samples each coordinate \(d\) from \(\mathcal{N}(s_{l,d}, \sigma_d^2)\) with rejection sampling in \([0, 1)\), where \(\sigma_d = \xi \sum_{e \ne l} \frac{|s_{e,d} - s_{l,d}|}{k - 1}\). Merges the \(m\) ants into \(T\), retains the best \(k\) solutions, and applies time-gated NelderMeadSearch to \(T[0]\).

docs.title: 3.1 Implicit Path-Relinking (IPR — src/mh/ipr.cpp)
docs.text: • Controlled Parameters (2, embedded): \(\alpha_{\text{block}} \in \{0.05, 0.10, 0.20\}\) and \(\text{typePR} \in \{0, \dots, 5\}\) (18 online states; offline uses \(\alpha = 0.10\), PR_ONE_WAY). Relinks elite pairs \((\mathbf{x}^s, \mathbf{x}^g)\) from SOLVER_POOL over contiguous key blocks across 6 strategies (see Algorithms & Control — IPR).

docs.title: 3.2 MultiStart (MultiStart — src/mh/multistart.cpp)
docs.text: • Parameter-free pure random-key sampler in \([0, 1)^n\), serving as an optimization baseline and continuous source of global diversity for SOLVER_POOL.

docs.title: API & Component Reference (rkolib)
docs.text: This document provides a technical reference for the core classes, data structures, plugin interfaces, scalarizers, Q-Learning routines, IO utilities, and all 15 metaheuristics implemented in RKOSolver (rkolib).

docs.text:

Central orchestrator class responsible for CLI parsing, YAML configuration loading, dynamic plugin loading, reference point initialization and synchronization, parallel OpenMP execution, and statistical output.

Thread-safe Singleton managing shared solver state across OpenMP threads: the elite solution pool (SOLVER_POOL), 64-byte cache-line-aligned per-thread RNGs (PaddedRng / SOLVER_RNG), run start timestamps, anti-drift pool re-scalarization, and cooperative stop flags (SOLVER_SHOULD_STOP).

docs.title: rkolib::core::IProblem
docs.text:
Header: include/rkolib/core/problem.hpp

Abstract base interface implemented by all dynamically loaded problem plugins.

namespace rkolib::core {
class IProblem {
public:
  virtual ~IProblem() = default;

  // Loads instance data from file
  virtual void load(const std::string &filename) = 0;

  // Transforms random-key vector (sol.rk) into a solution and populates sol.objs
  virtual void decode(TSol &sol) const = 0;

  // Returns number of random keys required by the decoder
  virtual int getDimension() const = 0;

  // Returns number of target objectives (1 = Single-Objective, >1 = Multi-Objective)
  virtual int getNumObjectives() const = 0;

  // Sets debug mode (0: silent, 1: detailed terminal output)
  virtual void setDebugMode(int debug) { (void)debug; }
};
}

docs.title: Plugin Registration Macro: REGISTER_RKO_PROBLEM
docs.text:
Exports create_problem and destroy_problem with C linkage for dlopen/dlsym:

#define REGISTER_RKO_PROBLEM(ProblemClass) \
  extern "C" { \
    EXPORT_PLUGIN rkolib::core::IProblem *create_problem() { \
      return new ProblemClass(); \
    } \
    EXPORT_PLUGIN void destroy_problem(rkolib::core::IProblem *p) { \
      delete p; \
    } \
  }

struct TRunData {
  int strategy;              // Local search strategy (1 = First Improvement, 2 = Best Improvement)
  int control;               // Parameter control mode (0 = Offline Tuning, 1 = Online Q-Learning)
  int MAXTIME;               // Maximum execution time in seconds
  int MAXRUNS;               // Maximum number of independent runs
  int debug;                 // Debug output level (0 = File output, 1 = Terminal logs)
  float restart;             // Restart threshold multiplier
  int sizePool;              // Base elite solution pool size (doubled when M > 1)
  int poolUpdateMethod = 0;  // Pool policy (0 = Cosine Diversity, 1 = NSGA-II, 2 = Spatial Niche Geometry)
  float tauMinNM = 0.005f;   // Minimum fraction of MAXTIME between Nelder-Mead calls
  float tauMaxNM = 0.20f;    // Maximum fraction of MAXTIME without a Nelder-Mead call
};

docs.title: Implementations
docs.text: Class Config Key (scalarization) Formula NormalizedWeightedTchebycheff "Tchebycheff" \(\max_k d_k + 10^{-4} \sum_k \frac{\max(0, f_k(x) - z^*_k)}{z^{\text{nad}}_k - z^*_k}\) WeightedSumScalarizer "WeightedSum" \(\sum_k w_k \cdot f_k(x)\) GiniScalarizer "Gini_Coefficient" \(\bar{d} \cdot (1 + G(d)) = \bar{d} + \frac{1}{2 M^2} \sum_i \sum_j \|d_i - d_j\|\) over normalized regrets \(d_k \ge 0\) LexicographicMinMaxScalarizer "Lexicographic_MinMax" \(\sum_{r=0}^{M-1} \gamma^{r} d_{(r)} + \frac{10^{-6}}{M}\sum_{r=1}^{M-1} d_{(r)}\) with sorted \(d_{(0)} \ge \dots \ge d_{(M-1)}\)

docs.title: 5. Q-Learning Control Engine
docs.text:
Header: include/rkolib/core/qlearning.hpp Implementation: src/core/qlearning.cpp

namespace rkolib::core {

// Builds the Cartesian state space and O(|S| * m) M/D/A adjacent action topology
void CreateStates(const std::vector<std::vector<double>> &parameters,
                  int &numStates, int numPar, std::vector<TState> &S);

// Selects an action using an epsilon-greedy policy
int ChooseAction(const std::vector<TState> &S, int st, double epsilon);

// Computes capped relative improvement in [0, delta_max] (default delta_max = 0.1)
double ComputeDelta(double oldBest, double newBest, double delta_max = 0.1);

// Improvement-based epsilon decay with floor epsilon_min (default 0.1)
void SetQLParameter(double &epsilon, double &lf, double &df, int MAXTIME,
                    float currentTime, float delta, double epsilon_min = 0.1);

// Cosine annealing with warm restarts (epsilon_max passed by reference)
void SetQLParameter(float currentTime, int &Ti, int &restartEpsilon,
                    float &epsilon_max, float epsilon_min,
                    double &epsilon, double &lf, double &df, int MAXTIME);

// Recomputes maxQ and maxA for state st
void UpdateMaxQ(std::vector<TState> &S, int st);

// Applies Bellman update, conditionally calls UpdateMaxQ, and transitions st -> st_1
void UpdateQValue(std::vector<TState> &S, int &st, int at,
                  double R, double lf, double df);

// Thread-safe Q-Table persistence (results/QTable_<method>.txt)
bool SaveQTable(const std::vector<TState> &S, int st,
                const std::string &method, const std::string &outDir = "results");
bool LoadQTable(std::vector<TState> &S,
                const std::string &method, const std::string &outDir = "results");

void PrintPolicy(const std::vector<TState> &S, int st);

} // namespace rkolib::core

docs.title: 6. Local Search, Pool Management & IO
docs.text: Headers: include/rkolib/core/method.hpp, include/rkolib/utils/io.hpp

docs.title: Core Search & Pool Functions (rkolib::core)
docs.text:
• CreatePoolSolutions(solver, sizePool): Two-pass pool initialization ensuring consolidated Ideal/Nadir reference points and clone mutation.
  • UpdatePoolSolutions(sol, method, debug, poolUpdateMethod): Thread-safe (pool_lock) elite pool update supporting Cosine Similarity diversity (0), NSGA-II (1), and Spatial Frontier Niche Geometry (2).
  • RVND(s, solver, strategy, RKorder): Randomized Variable Neighborhood Descent over SwapLS, InvertLS, and FareyLS.
  • NelderMeadSearch(x1, solver): Simplex search over random keys using thread-safe pool sampling (pool_lock).

docs.title: IO Utilities (rkolib::utils)
docs.text:
• WriteResults(...) / WriteMultiObjectiveResults(...): Appends single-objective (Results_RKO.csv) or multi-objective (Results_MO_RKO.csv) run statistics.
  • WriteSolution(...) / WriteSolutionScreen(...): Logs detailed global best solution and terminal summary.
  • PrintPoolSolutions(pool, dimension): Prints the formatted elite pool summary (OFV, MH, Best time, Objs, RK) to stdout.
  • WritePoolSolutions(algorithms, pool, instance, dimension, outDir = "results"): Appends the full elite pool to results/Pool_Solutions_RKO.txt.
  • WriteConvergenceLog(history, outDir = "results"): Exports timestamped incumbent improvement points to results/Convergence_Log.csv.
